summary: Built the tiered runner tools/run_tiers.py with its lists in tools/tiers.json. Tier 0 is 25 fast guarding modules, two of them run in part: 412 tests in 39 s. Tier 1 is tier 0 plus whatever imports a changed file; for a one-line change in agenda_qt.py it chose 5 modules and took 1m 46s. Tier 2 is the release: every module, the 22 window checks, the Rail Demo scene four ways, the name sweep and the release check's integrity sections. It took 11m 36s in the Graphite look and 11m 35s in the Kasandra look, with 1,160 tests and 0 failing in each. Each module, check or scene runs in its own child: an empty HOME and TMPDIR, nice 19, its own pid namespace (or a process group where the machine allows no namespace), two at a time, longest first, and it is killed at its time limit. Each tier writes tier<N>.json and logs under --out and prints one table and a last line ('0 failing' or the list). --against reports a change in a failure's message, not only in its state. Tier 2 reads FOCUSED_MODULES, ON_DEMAND_MODULES and UI_CHECKS from tools/check_hatch.py each time it runs. Added docs/CHECKS.md, one line in the README's Checks section and a pointer in docs/WINDOW_CHECKS.md. Added tests_integrated/test_run_tiers.py (12 tests). Both test_run_tiers and test_release_check pass in both looks. Timed every fixed wait in the window checks; no wait met the rule for a safe mechanical swap, so none was changed, and they are listed in docs/CHECKS.md.

new_tests: tests_integrated.test_run_tiers.TheLists.test_every_test_module_is_in_tier_2_in_both_looks_and_tier_0_is_a_part_of_it: every tests_integrated/test_*.py is in tier 2 in both looks, except the two modules that run both looks themselves, which run once. Tier 0 is a subset of tier 2 with no duplicates; every entry gives its reason; every class a partial entry names exists in its module.

tests_integrated.test_run_tiers.TheLists.test_tier_0_always_holds_what_guards_the_owner: her hand's rules, the memory rules, release integrity, the seed-is-current test, one name and the Kernel's scopes are all in tier 0.

tests_integrated.test_run_tiers.TheLists.test_tier_2_runs_the_gates_window_checks_and_the_scene_in_each_look_and_the_sweep_once: tier 2 runs exactly UI_CHECKS and the scene in each look, and the integrity sections and the name sweep once; a single-look run has every module.

tests_integrated.test_run_tiers.TheLists.test_tier_1_is_tier_0_when_nothing_changed_and_adds_what_imports_a_change: with no change, tier 1 is tier 0. On the real tree a change to tools/run_tiers.py chooses test_run_tiers and MANIFEST.json chooses nothing. A tier-0 module that runs only in part runs whole when a change chooses it.

tests_integrated.test_run_tiers.TheImportMap.test_a_test_is_chosen_by_what_it_imports_or_names_and_by_what_its_helpers_do: on a small invented tree, a test is chosen by what it imports (relative imports resolved, the package __init__ counted), by a patch-target string, by a path string and by a helper in tools/. The program's own imports are not followed. A file that does not parse still counts as itself.

tests_integrated.test_run_tiers.TheImportMap.test_a_file_that_is_not_python_is_followed_to_the_python_that_names_it_and_the_ignored_are_not: a changed .json file selects through the module that names it; changes under wip/ and to MANIFEST.json select nothing.

tests_integrated.test_run_tiers.TheImportMap.test_the_map_is_kept_and_read_again_only_where_a_file_changed: the import-map cache is written; nothing is parsed again when nothing changed; only the edited file is read again; a damaged cache is rebuilt.

tests_integrated.test_run_tiers.TheImportMap.test_the_changed_files_are_what_differs_from_the_commit_and_what_git_does_not_know: changed_files lists modified, deleted and untracked files; a ref that does not exist exits with words.

tests_integrated.test_run_tiers.TheRunner.test_each_module_in_a_child_of_its_own_a_failure_with_its_message_and_a_time_limit_is_a_failure: on an invented tree each child gets an empty HOME, the given look and offscreen. A failing module fails the run and keeps the assertion message. A module at its time limit is reported as TIMEOUT and counted as failing, and the grandchild it started does not outlive it. An import error is a failure. The last line is '0 failing' or the list.

tests_integrated.test_run_tiers.TheRunner.test_without_a_process_namespace_the_process_group_is_stopped_whole: the fallback for a machine where unshare cannot make a namespace (a normal user): the whole process group is killed at the time limit.

tests_integrated.test_run_tiers.TheRunner.test_the_run_writes_its_result_file_prints_one_table_and_fails_when_a_module_fails: main() writes tier0.json with a row per module (module, look, ran, failed, seconds), prints the table and the failing message, exits 1 on a failure and 0 with '0 failing', and refuses an --out inside the program folder without creating it.

tests_integrated.test_run_tiers.TheRunner.test_a_change_of_message_is_a_difference_and_the_same_failure_is_not: --against counts a failure whose words changed as a change (what compare_ui hid twice), and also reports a state that changed, a new run and a run that is missing.

numbers: Tier 0 wall time: 39.9 s, 39.4 s and 38.6 s in three runs (25 runs, 412 tests, 0 failing), plus 35 s in a fourth run on the final tree once the measured seconds were in tools/tiers.json. Measured with run_tiers.py 0 on a copy, two at a time, each child at nice 19 in its own pid namespace. Load average was 1.9 to 3.5 because another builder's two test processes ran alongside. The children's time added up to 75.8 s.

Tier 1 for a one-line change appended to workbench/agenda_qt.py: 1 min 46 s (106.3 s), 30 runs, 492 tests, 0 failing. It chose test_delete_words, test_hologram, test_kasandra_column, test_session_start and test_typewriter_faces. MANIFEST.json and the seed, which changed with the seed rebuild, are ignored by design. Measured with run_tiers.py 1 --changed HEAD on a copy made into a git repository.

Tier 2 in the Graphite look: 11 min 36 s (696.0 s), 100 runs, 1,160 tests, 22 window checks (220 steps), the scene 4 of 4, 0 failing. The children took 1,391 s between them: modules 920 s, window checks 372 s, scene 90 s, name sweep 5 s, check_release sections 4 s. Two at a time, wall time is half of that.
Tier 2 in the Kasandra look: 11 min 35 s (695.0 s), 100 runs, 1,160 tests, 0 failing. Run after the Graphite run, not alongside it.
Both looks in one run (--look both, tier 2's default): about 21 min, estimated from the two runs because the two both-look modules and the sweep are shared. Not measured.
Import map: 2.9 s to build for 688 Python files and 0.02 s from the cache. Measured with the tool's own functions on a copy.

Dependency rule, measured on the tree: following every import transitively chose 72 of 74 test modules for any of the 7 files tried. The rule kept (what a test and its own helpers in tests_integrated/ and tools/ import or name) chose 1 to 24 modules: 5 for agenda_qt.py, 1 for typed_pipeline.py, 24 for shell2.py.

Fixed waits in the window checks: 115 of 351 s spent in QTest.qWait (33%), measured by timing every qWait and sleep in one run of each of the 22 checks in the Graphite look. More than half: check_model_turn_ui 8.8 of 14.5 s (mostly condition waits already) and check_finder_ui 37 of 67 s (settle, about 400 times). Tier 0 sleeps 0.6 s in total.

Release checks outside the suite: 64.8 min at 0.8.2 (72.9 with the suite) against about 6.7 min per look now (tier 2 minus its modules: 1,391 - 920 = 471 child-seconds, about 3.9 min of wall time two at a time). The whole release tier, suite included, is 11.6 min per look, 23.2 min for both looks run one after the other.
decisions: Tier 1 follows what a test module and its own helpers in tests_integrated/ and tools/ import or name: imports anywhere in the file, patch-target strings and path strings, with each package __init__ counted. It does not follow the program's own imports. Reason: following them chose 72 of 74 modules for any change, because the window imports most of the program, and the task asks that a small change runs a small set. A change that reaches a test only through the window is left to tier 2. docs/CHECKS.md says so. A changed file that is not Python is followed to the Python files that name its path or file name.
Tier 1 also runs a window check when the check imports or names a changed file. The spec describes tier 1 as 'the window modules chosen by which files changed'.

Tier 2's module list is not copied into tiers.json. It is read from tools/check_hatch.py FOCUSED_MODULES plus ON_DEMAND_MODULES each time it runs, so a new module (for example from the guards builder) joins tier 2 automatically. test_run_tiers checks that every test_*.py file is included. UI_CHECKS and UI_CAPTURE_ENV are read from check_hatch.py each time too, as the task asked.
test_exact_math_solvers, an on-demand module, is in tier 2 because tier 2 means everything. It skips itself when SymPy and Z3 are missing.

In tier 2 with both looks, test_one_name and test_rail_demo_campaign run once, in the first look. Each already starts children in both looks itself, so a second run repeated about 200 s and judged nothing new. With a single look they run in that look. tiers.json gives the reason.

Tier 0 runs part of two modules by class: test_one_name (TheName, TheSweepItself, TheCode), whose window sweep takes about 2 minutes, and test_desk_acts (PureRules), the hand's rule over desk acts without a window. A test checks that the named classes exist.

Tier 0 membership: always the guarding modules the task named (scopes: test_conditions, test_network_watch, test_documents, test_cabinet_actions; her hand: test_stacy_hand and desk_acts PureRules; memory rules: test_resource_rules, test_memory_settings, test_model_settings; release integrity: test_release_check; seed current: test_project_desk; one name: test_one_name in part). Also change sets, continuing work and backup. Then, from kill_matrix.json per_module, every module with at least one unique kill and a base time under 7 s: stacy_hand, faces_find_light, joined_work, service_lifecycle, model_settings, kasandra, workspace_backup, release_check, cabinet, operations, continuing_work, change_sets, conditions, resource_rules, stacy_start, deployment. test_line_rules and test_colour_vision were added for the 0.8.4 rules they pin. test_graphite (7.15 s) and test_slate_reasoning (12 s) were left out for time.

Tier 2 also runs tools/check_release.py once, for the payload, seed, registry and privacy sections: the spec puts 'the gate' in tier 2. It runs tools/name_sweep.py once for the code; the window sweep is test_one_name in the suite.
In the scene unit a Blocked case counts as failing, because a release check that did not run is not a pass. On Rail Demo, Blocked happens only when pypdf or Poppler is missing.

Isolation is nice 19 plus 'unshare --pid --fork --mount-proc --kill-child' when a quick probe shows unshare works (as root here). Otherwise the child gets its own process group, and the whole group is killed at the time limit. The result file records which was used. QT_QPA_PLATFORM is forced to offscreen. ARC1_WORKBENCH_CONFIG_HOME, ARC_LEDGER_CONCERN, ARC_LEDGER_XSESSION, the XDG_*_HOME folders and PYTHONPATH are removed from each child's environment.
--out defaults to a new temporary folder, and an --out inside the program folder is refused. Reason: an earlier gate run wrote captures into the tree (4873b67), and campaign.py refuses the same.
The import-map cache is kept in the user's cache folder ($XDG_CACHE_HOME or ~/.cache/graphite-tiers, keyed by the program folder's path), not in the program folder, so packaging never ships it.

compare_ui lives only in scratch, so it was not changed. The equivalent here: each row keeps its failing tests and the last line of what each raised, and --against EARLIER.json reports a changed message as a difference.
check_release.py --self-test and --ui are left as they were. They remain the shipped single entry for integrity; tier 2 is the release tier.
The test_run_tiers line in FOCUSED_MODULES is on its own line after test_colour_vision, with its own comment and a blank line above, away from the other builders' lines.
not_done: No fixed wait was replaced with a wait for a condition. Measured: none of the 25 tier-0 units waits (test_network_watch has two 0.3 s sleeps for a real capture thread). Of the window checks, only check_model_turn_ui and check_finder_ui wait more than half their time. model_turn's waits are already condition waits. finder's settle() runs about 400 times during the width and size sweeps, waiting for deferred layouts and timers that have no single condition, so the swap is not mechanical or safe. Halving it would save about 9 s per look. Listed and left: check_operations_ui's qWait(400) after each slider key and its qWait(2100) for the meters' timer (2.9 of 8.8 s), and the settles in check_context_menu_ui (9.4 of 21 s) and check_agent_ui (6.8 of 18 s).

Step 2 of release-checks.md was not done beyond the cheap items: no new scenes P02 (mouse path), P03 (her hand) or P04 (meters and pane), and the probes' remaining checks were not moved into test_desk_acts. docs/CHECKS.md names these as not done.
The probes and the crawler are not in tier 2. They lived only in scratch, and docs/CHECKS.md says so.
Tier 2 with --look both was not measured as a single run. The two looks were measured one after the other, as the task asked; the single run is estimated at about 21 min.

The guards builder's new tests are not in tier 0. If they land in existing tier-0 modules (test_project_desk, test_release_check, test_stacy_hand, test_resource_rules and others) they run there. A new module joins tier 2 automatically; to put it in tier 0, add one entry with a reason to tools/tiers.json '0'.
The process-group fallback is tested with a fake module but was not run on a machine without unshare. Nothing ran on the owner's ThinkPad.
tiers.json still lists test_run_tiers at 11 s; with the 12th test it measured 18 s. The value only affects run order and was not changed after the last test run.
release_note: The checks now run in three tiers from one command, python3 tools/run_tiers.py 0, 1 or 2. Tier 0 runs the 25 fastest modules that guard the most, including every test guarding the owner, and took 39 seconds here. Tier 1 adds the tests that use the files you changed: 1 minute 46 seconds for a one-line change. Tier 2 is the release: every test, the 22 window checks and the scene on Rail Demo in both looks, plus the name sweep. It took 11 minutes 36 seconds per look here (23 minutes for both looks) with 0 failing, against 73 minutes for the release checks at 0.8.2. The probes and the crawler, which were never part of the program and never caught a fault at a release, are no longer run. docs/CHECKS.md describes each tier and when to run it.
